# `set_focal_length`

<!-- Generated by tools/gen_cards.py from catalog/. Do not edit by hand. -->

Store a new focal-length value in the device settings (64-bit build); the 32-bit build only acknowledges.

## Summary

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Kind | method (client sends) |
| Grade | MUTATOR / probable (64-bit build; 32-bit build probable); the 32-bit handler as read is a no-op acknowledgement |
| Side-effect tier | C |
| Confidence | READ |
| Basis | static analysis of firmware 9.31, handler @0xceed0, SetFocalLen @0x11c9b0 (64-bit build); 32-bit handler @0x65e14 |

Takes one number (a scalar, or the first element of an array) and passes it to the focal-length setter, which overwrites the in-memory focal-length setting and writes a log line. No range or sign check is made. The 64-bit build accepts an integer or a real and stores it as a 32-bit float. The 32-bit build accepts only an integer tag, never reads or applies the payload, and acknowledges with result 0. The value is in millimetres (factory default 250); it drives the plate scale, pixel size (micrometres) x 206.265 x bin / focal length. The malformed-parameter reply uses the integer-parameter message even though reals are accepted.

Side effects: 64-bit build: overwrites the shared focal-length setting in memory and logs; no demonstrated configuration persistence and no motor operation. 32-bit build: none.

## Request params

| Name | Type | Required | Default | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | any | yes | - | Client-chosen request identifier, echoed in the reply as parsed (same JSON type). Required; a request without one is rejected with code 200. The device accepts any JSON value: zero, negative, string, null, boolean and composite ids are all treated as real requests, not notifications. Clients SHOULD use an integer or a string and SHOULD keep ids unique among outstanding requests. On early dispatcher errors (100, 200) the reply carries id null. [READ] |
| `method` | string | yes | - | Fixed value `"set_focal_length"`. [READ] |
| `params` | number\|array | yes | - | The focal-length number as a bare scalar or as the first element of an array. Absent, empty array, null or non-number gives 104. The 32-bit build requires an integer. No keys, no default, no range check. Millimetres. [READ] |

| `Timestamp` | string | no | - | (both) Decimal string `<seconds>.<nanoseconds>` with exactly nine fractional digits, formatted with `%ld.%09ld` from clock_gettime clock id 1. Linux clock id 1 is CLOCK_MONOTONIC, so the value is monotonic time, not wall-clock or Unix time (INFERRED from the clock id). ## Errors

| Code | Trigger | Label |
|---|---|---|
| 104 | Parameter absent, empty, null or not a number (64-bit); not an integer (32-bit) | `expected int param` |
| 200 | Dispatcher: request has no id | `invalid id` |
| 100 | Dispatcher: method missing or not a string | `invalid request` |

The focal-length setter itself never fails.

## Example

Request, request - Array form (values invented):

```json
{"id":41,"method":"set_focal_length","params":[250]}
```

Request, scalar-real - Scalar real form, 64-bit build only (value invented):

```json
{"id":42,"method":"set_focal_length","params":250.5}
```

Reply, ok:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"set_focal_length","result":0,"code":0,"id":41}
```

Reply, error:

```json
{"jsonrpc":"2.0","Timestamp":"1234.123456789","method":"set_focal_length","error":"expected int param","code":104,"id":43}
```
